text:
Year two is going differently for Berkly Catton. NHL.com called it "Catton Finding His Groove in Year 2," and the line agrees: 8 goals and 17 points in 19 games, already matching the 17 points he had in 66 games as a rookie. He's playing 15:09 a night, up from 12:56, with a bigger slice of the power play.

Our numbers call the hot run partly real. Seattle takes 54.6% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice, 12 points better than without him, and his skating sits in the 96th percentile for top speed per NHL EDGE. But 8 goals on 3.5 expected, shooting 28%, is a rate that rarely lasts, and his teammates have scored 6.1 more goals than expected with him out there.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 52% of his shots coming off the rush last season, which fits the speed. For context, forwards drafted 6th to 10th since 2005 averaged a median 0.41 points a game in their first full season; he's at 0.89. Watch the shot volume: 29 shots in 19 games is low for this kind of scoring.
